# zlarft

> Form the triangular factor T of a complex block reflector H of order N.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import zlarft from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/zlarft';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
zlarft( order, direct, storev, N, K, V, LDV, TAU, strideTAU, T, LDT ) → Complex128Array
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `direct` | `"forward" \| "backward"` | `'forward'` or `'backward'` |
| `storev` | `"columnwise" \| "rowwise"` | `'columnwise'` or `'rowwise'` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the block reflector |
| `K` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of elementary reflectors |
| `V` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × K</sub> | Input matrix |
| ↳ `LDV` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `V` |
| `TAU` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length K</sub> | Input array |
| ↳ `strideTAU` | `integer` | `TAU` stride length |
| `T` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>K × K</sub> | **out** · Input matrix |
| ↳ `LDT` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `T` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `direct`: Specifies the order in which the elementary reflectors are multiplied to form the block reflector:

  -   `= 'F'`: $H = H(1)$ H(2) . . . H(k) (Forward)
  -   `= 'B'`: $H = H(k)$ . . . H(2) H(1) (Backward)
- `storev`: Specifies how the vectors which define the elementary reflectors are stored (see also Further Details):

  -   `= 'C'`: columnwise
  -   `= 'R'`: rowwise
- `N`: The order of the block reflector H. $N \ge 0$.
- `K`: The order of the triangular factor T (= the number of elementary reflectors). $K \ge 1$.
- `V`: (`LDV`,N) if `STOREV = 'R'` The matrix V. See further details.
- `TAU`: `TAU(i)` must contain the scalar factor of the elementary reflector H(i).
- `T`: The k by k triangular factor T of the block reflector. If `DIRECT = 'F'`, T is upper triangular; if `DIRECT = 'B'`, T is lower triangular. The rest of the array is not used.

</details>

**Returns** `Complex128Array`: `T`

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "forward", "backward"
- `TypeError` third argument must be one of the following: "columnwise", "rowwise"

### Strided (strided) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
zlarft.strided(
    direct, storev,
    N, K,
    V, strideV1, strideV2, offsetV,
    TAU, strideTAU, offsetTAU,
    T, strideT1, strideT2, offsetT
) → Complex128Array
```

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `direct` | `"forward" \| "backward"` | `'forward'` or `'backward'` |
| `storev` | `"columnwise" \| "rowwise"` | `'columnwise'` or `'rowwise'` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the block reflector |
| `K` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of elementary reflectors |
| `V` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × K</sub> | Matrix of reflector vectors |
| ↳ `strideV1` | `integer` | Stride of first dim of V (complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideV2` | `integer` | Stride of second dim of V (complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetV` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for V (in complex elements) |
| `TAU` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length K</sub> | Array of scalar factors |
| ↳ `strideTAU` | `integer` | Stride for TAU (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetTAU` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for TAU (in complex elements) |
| `T` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>K × K</sub> | **out** · Output triangular matrix |
| ↳ `strideT1` | `integer` | Stride of first dim of T (complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideT2` | `integer` | Stride of second dim of T (complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetT` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for T (in complex elements) |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `direct`: Specifies the order in which the elementary reflectors are multiplied to form the block reflector:

  -   `= 'F'`: $H = H(1)$ H(2) . . . H(k) (Forward)
  -   `= 'B'`: $H = H(k)$ . . . H(2) H(1) (Backward)
- `storev`: Specifies how the vectors which define the elementary reflectors are stored (see also Further Details):

  -   `= 'C'`: columnwise
  -   `= 'R'`: rowwise
- `N`: The order of the block reflector H. $N \ge 0$.
- `K`: The order of the triangular factor T (= the number of elementary reflectors). $K \ge 1$.
- `V`: (`LDV`,N) if `STOREV = 'R'` The matrix V. See further details.
- `TAU`: `TAU(i)` must contain the scalar factor of the elementary reflector H(i).
- `T`: The k by k triangular factor T of the block reflector. If `DIRECT = 'F'`, T is upper triangular; if `DIRECT = 'B'`, T is lower triangular. The rest of the array is not used.

</details>

**Returns** `Complex128Array`: `T`

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "forward", "backward"
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "columnwise", "rowwise"
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer

</section>

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import discreteUniform from '@stdlib/random/array/discrete-uniform/lib/index.js';
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import reinterpret from '@stdlib/strided/base/reinterpret-complex128/lib/index.js';
import zlarft from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/zlarft';

/** @type {{ dtype: 'float64' }} */
const opts = {
	'dtype': 'float64'
};
const N = 3;
const K = 2;
const V = new Complex128Array( discreteUniform( 2 * N * K, -10, 10, opts ) );
const TAU = new Complex128Array( discreteUniform( 2 * K, -1, 1, opts ) );
let T = new Complex128Array( K * K );

// Using the standard interface:
zlarft( 'column-major', 'forward', 'columnwise', N, K, V, N, TAU, 1, T, K );
console.log( reinterpret( T, 0 ) ); // eslint-disable-line no-console

// Using the strided interface:
T = new Complex128Array( K * K );
zlarft.strided( 'forward', 'columnwise', N, K, V, 1, N, 0, TAU, 1, 0, T, 1, K, 0 );
console.log( reinterpret( T, 0 ) ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `ZLARFT`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

ZLARFT forms the triangular factor T of a complex block reflector H of order n, which is defined as a product of k elementary reflectors.

If `DIRECT = 'F'`, $H = H(1)$ H(2) . . . H(k) and T is upper triangular;

If `DIRECT = 'B'`, $H = H(k)$ . . . H(2) H(1) and T is lower triangular.

If `STOREV = 'C'`, the vector which defines the elementary reflector H(i) is stored in the i-th column of the array V, and

$$
H = I - V \, T \, V^H
$$

If `STOREV = 'R'`, the vector which defines the elementary reflector H(i) is stored in the i-th row of the array V, and

$$
H = I - V^H \, T \, V
$$

### Further Details

The shape of the matrix V and the storage of the vectors which define the H(i) is best illustrated by the following example with $n = 5$ and $k = 3$. The elements equal to 1 are not stored.

`DIRECT = 'F'` and `STOREV = 'C'`: `DIRECT = 'F'` and `STOREV = 'R'`:

$$
V = \begin{pmatrix} 1 &  &  \\ v_{1} & 1 &  \\ v_{1} & v_{2} & 1 \\ v_{1} & v_{2} & v_{3} \\ v_{1} & v_{2} & v_{3} \end{pmatrix} V = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & v_{1} & v_{1} & v_{1} & v_{1} \\  & 1 & v_{2} & v_{2} & v_{2} \\  &  & 1 & v_{3} & v_{3} \end{pmatrix}
$$

`DIRECT = 'B'` and `STOREV = 'C'`: `DIRECT = 'B'` and `STOREV = 'R'`:

$$
V = \begin{pmatrix} v_{1} & v_{2} & v_{3} \\ v_{1} & v_{2} & v_{3} \\ 1 & v_{2} & v_{3} \\  & 1 & v_{3} \\  &  & 1 \end{pmatrix} V = \begin{pmatrix} v_{1} & v_{1} & 1 &  &  \\ v_{2} & v_{2} & v_{2} & 1 &  \\ v_{3} & v_{3} & v_{3} & v_{3} & 1 \end{pmatrix}
$$

</section>
